rows.author: C126
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING AN ACROSS-THE-BOAR D INCREASE IN DAILY WAGES TO ALL PRIVATE SECTOR WORKERS NATIONWIDE TAKING INTO CONSIDERATION NATIONAL CONSUMER PRICE INDEX (CPI) AND GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT (GDP) INCREASES, WITH THE YEAR 1991 AS THE BASE YEAR
rows.abstract: The daily wages of all private sector workers under existing laws shall be increased across-the-boar d by the sum of the Wage Recovery and Fair Share where Wage Recovery and Fair Share are computed as follws: (1) Wage Recovery = regional wage in 1991 x national CPI increase - current regional minimum wage; and (2)  Fair Share = regional minimum wage in 1991 x average annual national GDP growth x 9 years. Hence. New Minimum Wage = Current Regional Minimum Wage + Wage Recovery + Fair Share: Provided, That the measure of the CPI shall consider the projected rise in prices until the end of the year 2000.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2000-09-25

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE BARANGAY INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT APPROACH FOR NUTRITION IMPROVEMENT (BIDANI) OF THE RURAL POOR AS A NETWORK PROGRAM OF THE PARTICIPATING STATE COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "BIDANI Act of 2000." Rationale: It is the policy of the State to recognize nutrition as a basic human right, just as the right to health and to life are. Towards this end, the state shall promote vigorously the importance of nutrition as a public good and public concern which can be achieved only through multi-sectoral efforts and democratic process.  It shall work towards the provision of the nutritional needs of the sector of Filipino society who are deprived of the said right. Moreover, thestate shall give utmost support to programs and projects that are responsive to the nutritional needs of the people.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2000-10-02

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CERTAIN BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES TO SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICS TEACHERS
rows.abstract: "Developing Globally Competitive Science and Mathematics Teachers Act." The attached bill proposes to provide measures that will attract bright students in mathematics and science to pursue a career in science teaching, to enable them to advance intheir specialization, sustain their interest in this field, and encourage them to stay in science teaching.  It also provides measures that will continually upgrade the competence of those who are already in science teaching.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2000-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 205, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ORIGINAL CHARTER OF THE DEVELOPMENT ACADEMY OF THE PHILIPPINES (DAP)
rows.abstract: Rationale: Over the years. the Academy's concerns have expanded.  In its desire to continuously support the thrusts and initiatives of the nation to provide development services, it has aligned its programs and projects by working as partner not only with government but the private sector and civil society as  well. The Academy, as a "think tank" and capability builder of government, needs to be competitive in the market by making its compensation plan attractive and enticing to personnel. Thisis in the hope that the Academy will constantly and continuously contribute to the enhancement and development of the country.

rows.author: C107
rows.title_full: AN ACT REVISING THE EXCISE TAX SYSTEM ON FERMENTED LIQUORS, CIGARS AND CIGARETTES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 143 AND 145 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to revise the excise taxation imposed on fermented liquor, cigar and cigarettes from specific to ad valorem tax system. It proposes the following rate of tax based on the constructive brewer's/manufa cturer's or importer's wholesaleprice or the actual brewer's/manufa cturer's or importer's wholesale price, whichever is higher: on fermented liquors: a three-tiered rate of 40%, 45% and 50%, on cigars, a rate of 10%, on cigarettes packed by hand, a rate of 15% and on cigarettes packed by machine, a three-tiered rate of 40%, 60% and 70%.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2000-10-02
